text.tspan: People continue their journey in rainy weather.
There is more than one way to change our plans. In my experience, practical preparation and attention
to others are two useful starting points.
One reason is that a backup plan makes a change less disappointing. For instance, we choose a
museum when rain makes the outdoor walk uncomfortable. This prevents a small difficulty from taking
over the experience. It also leaves us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that telling other people early helps everyone adjust. For example, we send a clear
message about the new meeting place before anyone leaves home. This approach recognises that the
experience belongs to more than one person and that different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control
every detail. We can make a sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the
conclusion. Each body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the
argument rather than introduce a new proposal.
Persuade a group to change how they change our plans. Support your recommendation with two different reasons and a
practical example of each. Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion.
